description: A small brown mushroom with a caramel to chestnut cap 2-5 cm across and a distinctly wavy margin, fading to pale buff when dry. It bruises blue-green where handled. The stem is white and the spore print is purple-brown.
habitat: Grows in clusters on wood chips, mulch and garden beds, often in towns.
lookalikes: Galerina marginata (deadly): rusty-brown spore print and a ring or ring zone on the stem
safety_notes: PSYCHOACTIVE, WITH DEADLY LOOKALIKES: contains psilocybin and psilocin. Effects are unpredictable and can include fear, panic and lasting distress. The larger danger is misidentification, because deadly mushrooms look similar. Psilocybin is a controlled substance in many countries, including Canada and the United States; laws vary and are changing. Listed for identification and safety only. Never eat a wild mushroom on an app's word.
